entries.name: Ed Lazar

expected.charges: Contempt of court for the Everyman I voyage toward the Pacific nuclear-testing area.
expected.sentence: Sentenced June 7, 1962 to 30 days for contempt. Swann, who helped organize the voyage, confirms the three sailors spent an extended period in jail. The complete custody total and release date remain unresolved.

entries.rationale: May 28, 1962 AP report explicitly says Lazar was jailed overnight after the Saturday seizure and appeared Sunday, May 27, refusing bail. Add the verified initial custody start only. No assumption of uninterrupted custody or calculated release date.

entries.name: Samuel Reynier Tyson

expected.charges: Contempt of federal court order prohibiting the Everyman nuclear-test protest voyage
expected.sentence: Six-month contempt sentence in 1962; six months served according to his obituary. A contemporary Santa Rita letter reports his solitary confinement. Exact admission and release dates are unverified.

entries.rationale: L’Adunata dei Refrattari, July 26, 1962, page 2 explicitly names all five defendants and dates their six-month sentencing to July 11. Refine the existing July sentencing month to that day. This does not establish entry into custody or release. The article appears to conflate the Everyman boat designations, so no voyage or arrest date is imported from it.
